topStories.headline: Fisherman's Wharf Posts Record-Breaking July 4th Weekend, Hotels Sold Out
topStories.dek: Early business reports from the Fisherman's Wharf Community Benefit District show record sales, sold-out hotels, and surging restaurant revenue following Independence Day.
topStories.body:
Fisherman's Wharf is celebrating a banner Independence Day weekend, with early feedback from hotels, restaurants, retailers, and attractions pointing to a major boost in business activity across San Francisco's historic waterfront. The Fisherman's Wharf Community Benefit District reported on July 9 that the holiday weekend delivered significant increases in revenue and record-setting sales for many businesses.

The Argonaut Hotel and The Zephyr Hotel were both sold out over the holiday weekend. The Argonaut also reported its strongest July 4th performance since 2016. Several PIER 39 tenants reported record July 4th holiday sales, while Cioppino's Restaurant — located in Fisherman's Wharf toward Aquatic Park — reported that sales on July 4 were up 48% compared with the prior year, and up 19% for the Wednesday-through-Sunday holiday period. Bay Company reported sales up 100% on July 4 compared with the same day in 2025.

Business owners noted that the reopening of Maritime Park grass areas, which had been closed the prior year, may have contributed to the strong performance. New for 2026, San Francisco expanded its fireworks display in honor of America's 250th anniversary by adding a second launch site from the Golden Gate Bridge alongside the traditional barges near PIER 39 and Aquatic Park, drawing even larger crowds to the northern waterfront.

Bri Maughan, Executive Director of the Fisherman's Wharf Community Benefit District, attributed the success to the city's investment in public spaces. The strong July 4th results underscore the continued resurgence of Fisherman's Wharf as one of San Francisco's most important visitor destinations and economic engines.

topStories.headline: Park Tavern Closes for Good After 15 Years Overlooking Washington Square
topStories.dek: The North Beach bistro co-led by celebrity chef Jonathan Waxman served its last meal on June 21, leaving a prominent corner at 1652 Stockton St. vacant.
topStories.body:
Park Tavern, the American bistro that for 15 years was one of North Beach's most closely watched dining rooms, closed permanently on June 21, 2026. The restaurant operated at 1652 Stockton Street, directly across from Washington Square Park, and had been a neighborhood anchor since opening in the fall of 2011.

The closure caps a volatile chapter for the restaurant, which earned national attention and a James Beard Foundation semifinalist nomination for Best New Restaurant in its very first year. Park Tavern subsequently faced ownership disputes, pandemic closures, and financial difficulties. A revival launched in November 2024 under celebrity chef Jonathan Waxman and fifth-generation San Franciscan James Nicholas III ultimately could not sustain itself.

"After nearly 20 wonderful years on Washington Square, Park Tavern celebrated its final service on Sunday, June 21," the restaurant's website states. "We are incredibly grateful to our team, our guests, and this amazing community for making Park Tavern such a special place." The 1652 Stockton St. space — formerly home to the legendary Moose's — remains one of North Beach's most prominent dining locations, and speculation about its next occupant is already underway among neighborhood regulars.

topStories.headline: SF Marathon Brings Road Closures to Embarcadero and Fisherman's Wharf This Sunday
topStories.dek: The 49th San Francisco Marathon on July 26 routes 30,000 runners past the northern waterfront, with Embarcadero and Jefferson Street closures lasting through early afternoon.
topStories.body:
The 49th annual San Francisco Marathon takes place this Sunday, July 26, with its sold-out full marathon course running directly through the North Waterfront cluster. Runners will start at 5:15 a.m. at Embarcadero and Market Street, passing through Fisherman's Wharf — including Jefferson Street between Powell and Hyde — before heading to Marina Green, Crissy Field, and across the Golden Gate Bridge.

Residents and visitors should expect significant street impacts. Northbound Embarcadero and King Street will be closed from 3rd Street to Broadway starting just after midnight, with closures lasting through approximately 3 p.m. Jefferson Street in Fisherman's Wharf will be closed to vehicles when runners are present, from approximately 5 a.m. to 10:30 a.m. SFMTA is advising riders on multiple Muni lines to expect reroutes and delays throughout the morning.

The course is USATF-certified and an official Boston Marathon qualifier. Runner's World has named it one of the 12 best summer marathons. The full marathon, half marathons, 10K, and 5K all start and finish along the Embarcadero waterfront. With the 50th edition due in 2027, Sunday's race is the last before the event reaches its half-century milestone. Spectators are welcome along the waterfront route; public transit is strongly recommended.

events.title: San Francisco Marathon — Full Marathon, Half, 10K & 5K
events.description: The 49th SF Marathon routes thousands of runners along the Embarcadero and through Fisherman's Wharf before crossing the Golden Gate Bridge. Road closures affect the northern waterfront from midnight through early afternoon; public transit strongly recommended.

events.title: "Dear San Francisco" at Club Fugazi — Ongoing Summer Run
events.location: Club Fugazi, 678 Green Street, North Beach
events.description: The acclaimed cirque-style show by The 7 Fingers continues its summer run at the historic Club Fugazi, former home of Beach Blanket Babylon. The production features world-class acrobatics, live music, and a love letter to San Francisco's history, with tickets from $86.90.

events.title: Exploratorium Life in Space Festival
events.location: Exploratorium, Pier 15, Embarcadero at Green Street
events.description: A festive weekend of space science, discovery, and hands-on activities at the Exploratorium, including Storytime Science for Kids (Space Is the Place) on Saturday at noon. General admission required; special events may require separate tickets.

events.title: Exploratorium After Dark: Out of This World (18+)
events.location: Exploratorium, Pier 15, Embarcadero at Green Street
events.description: Adults-only evening at the Exploratorium exploring the possibility of life beyond Earth, featuring SETI scientists and interactive exhibits. Separate tickets required from general daytime admission.

events.title: Critical Mass Bike Ride
events.location: Embarcadero Plaza, foot of Market Street
events.description: San Francisco's beloved monthly mass bicycle ride departs from Embarcadero Plaza on the last Friday of every month, winding through city streets with hundreds of cyclists. Free and open to all riders.

events.title: Circus Bella Free Summer Tour — North Beach Stop
events.location: North Beach (exact location TBA — check circusbella.org)
events.description: Circus Bella's free 2026 summer tour brings acrobats, aerialists, jugglers, clowns, and a live 6-piece band to North Beach for a 65-minute all-ages show. A $25 donation is suggested; bring a blanket or folding chair.

moreNews.headline: Bastille Day Festival Drew Crowds to Embarcadero Plaza on July 18
moreNews.body: The 7th annual Celebrate Bastille Day SF Festival was held at Embarcadero Plaza on Saturday, July 18, running from 11 AM to 6 PM. Organized by the Official Committee of French-American Organizations of Northern California, the free outdoor festival featured French food, wine, beer, art, culture, and live entertainment. Billed as the largest public celebration of France's National Day in the San Francisco Bay Area, the event marked the 250-year friendship between France and the United States.

moreNews.headline: SF Marathon's 5K Warmed Up the Waterfront on Saturday
moreNews.body: The Saturday 5K kick-off to SF Marathon weekend took place July 25 along the Embarcadero, starting and finishing at Embarcadero and Washington Street. The flat, fast, and scenic course offered runners waterfront views of iconic SF architecture. The 5K is part of a full race weekend that includes the ultra marathon, full marathon, two half marathons, and a 10K on Sunday, July 26, all starting and finishing along the Embarcadero.

moreNews.headline: Telegraph Hill's 'Hill Bomb' Skateboard Event Draws Police Presence in April
moreNews.body: An unsanctioned "Hill Bomb" skateboarding event took place on Montgomery Street on the slopes of Telegraph Hill in mid-April 2026, drawing more police officers than participants, according to reports. The event was organized under the banner "Frisco Hill Bomb" after the traditional Dolores Street location was deterred by speed bumps installed by the city. Participants and organizers expressed hope for better coordination with city officials to eventually sanction a safer version of the event.

restaurants.name: Scoma's Restaurant
restaurants.description: Family-owned for three generations since 1965, Scoma's is a Fisherman's Wharf icon serving pier-to-plate seafood on its own working waterfront pier, with complimentary valet parking.
restaurants.address: Pier 47, 1 Al Scoma Way, Fisherman's Wharf

restaurants.name: Bistro Boudin at Fisherman's Wharf
restaurants.description: San Francisco's most famous sourdough bakery, founded in 1849, with a full-service waterfront restaurant on the upper level offering bay views and classic bread-bowl chowder.

restaurants.name: Cioppino's Restaurant
restaurants.description: Waterfront seafood restaurant at Fisherman's Wharf near Aquatic Park, celebrated for its cioppino and fresh catch, and a standout performer in the 2026 July 4th holiday weekend.

restaurants.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
restaurants.description: World-champion pizzaiolo Tony Gemignani's flagship North Beach restaurant, serving multiple styles of award-winning pizza from wood-fired and coal-fired ovens.

restaurants.name: Original Joe's North Beach
restaurants.description: A beloved San Francisco institution originally founded in 1937, serving hearty Italian-American classics in a retro, open-kitchen setting on Union Street.

restaurants.name: Cafe Zoetrope
restaurants.description: Francis Ford Coppola's café housed in the landmark 1907 Columbus Tower, offering Italian food, Coppola family wines, and a cinematic atmosphere filled with movie memorabilia.

restaurants.name: Caffe Trieste
restaurants.description: The first espresso house on the West Coast, open since 1956, beloved by Beat Generation writers and still serving Italian-style coffee and pastries in its original North Beach location.

restaurants.name: Il Casaro Pizzeria & Mozzarella Bar
restaurants.description: A North Beach favorite for gorgeous Neapolitan pies with hand-pulled mozzarella and a casual, lively atmosphere on Columbus Avenue.

restaurants.name: Barbara Pinseria and Cocktail Bar
restaurants.description: Sister restaurant to Il Casaro, serving rustic Roman-style pizza (pinsa) and craft cocktails including classic Campari spritzes in a relaxed Columbus Ave setting.

restaurants.name: Sotto Mare
restaurants.description: A beloved neighborhood classic on Green Street serving straightforward, delicious Northern Italian-style seafood in an unpretentious, always-busy dining room.

restaurants.name: Golden Boy Pizza
restaurants.description: A North Beach institution since 1978, Golden Boy serves thick Sicilian-style pizza slices from a cash-only counter on Green Street, especially popular late at night.

restaurants.name: Vesuvio Café
restaurants.description: A North Beach landmark since 1948, Vesuvio was a favorite haunt of Jack Kerouac and Allen Ginsberg and still serves drinks next door to City Lights Bookstore.

restaurants.name: Comstock Saloon
restaurants.type: Historic cocktail bar with live jazz
restaurants.description: A beautifully restored 1907 saloon in North Beach offering classic and craft cocktails, live jazz music several nights a week, and a vintage San Francisco atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Mama's on Washington Square
restaurants.description: A North Beach institution famous for long weekend lines, exceptional French toast, creative egg dishes, and freshly baked pastries overlooking Washington Square Park.

restaurants.name: Equal Parts SF
restaurants.description: A newer North Beach arrival bringing California-inflected dishes and creative cocktails to the historic Old Spaghetti Factory space at 478 Green Street, with a plant-filled interior and outdoor patio.

restaurants.name: Liguria Bakery
restaurants.description: A fourth-generation North Beach institution since 1911, Liguria sells only focaccia — in a handful of flavors — and routinely sells out by early morning.

restaurants.name: Tosca Cafe
restaurants.description: A storied North Beach bar founded in 1919, Tosca Cafe was redesigned by Ken Fulk and features an Italian-focused menu alongside its famous opera-on-the-jukebox atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Blue Mermaid Chowder House & Bar
restaurants.description: Located inside the Argonaut Hotel at Fisherman's Wharf, Blue Mermaid serves three kinds of chowder, steamed mussels, and fresh fish of the day in a nautical setting.

restaurants.name: Brick & Beam
restaurants.description: The Hyatt Centric Fisherman's Wharf's on-site restaurant and bar, serving local culinary favorites, Napa Valley wines, and craft cocktails in a striking brick-and-steel nautical setting.

hotels.name: Argonaut Hotel
hotels.description: A Kimpton property housed in a former 1907 canning factory at the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park, featuring nautical-themed rooms and direct access to Aquatic Park; reported its strongest July 4th performance since 2016.

hotels.name: Hotel Zephyr San Francisco
hotels.description: A playful, maritime-inspired boutique hotel near Fisherman's Wharf with a large outdoor courtyard featuring games and fire pits, sold out over the July 4th holiday weekend.

hotels.name: Hotel Zoe Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A stylish boutique hotel offering complimentary bicycle rentals, a courtyard with fire pits and free s'mores nightly, and in-house restaurant Pescatore Trattoria.

hotels.name: Hyatt Centric Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A 316-room hotel near Pier 39 with nautically themed rooms, a heated outdoor pool and hot tub, and the on-site Brick & Beam restaurant and bar.

hotels.name: San Francisco Marriott Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A large full-service Marriott near Pier 39 with the on-site Red Fin Restaurant & Lounge, a fitness center, and meeting spaces for business and leisure travelers.

hotels.name: Hotel Riu Plaza Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A 4-star hotel at Fisherman's Wharf rated 9.0 by guests, offering modern rooms and easy walkability to Pier 39, Ghirardelli Square, and waterfront attractions.

hotels.name: Hotel Caza Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: A crisply designed family-friendly hotel at Fisherman's Wharf with an in-house bar and convenient walking access to the neighborhood's waterfront attractions.

hotels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites San Francisco Fishermans Wharf by IHG
hotels.description: A conveniently located mid-scale IHG property at Fisherman's Wharf offering comfortable rooms, complimentary breakfast, and easy access to the waterfront.

shops.name: City Lights Booksellers & Publishers
shops.description: Founded by poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti in 1953, City Lights is the nation's first all-paperback bookstore, a San Francisco Historic Landmark, and publisher of Allen Ginsberg's Howl — open daily 10 AM to 10 PM across three floors.

shops.name: The Beat Museum
shops.type: Museum, bookstore, and Beat Generation archive
shops.description: Located at 540 Broadway across from City Lights, The Beat Museum houses memorabilia, manuscripts, and personal effects of Jack Kerouac, Allen Ginsberg, and other Beat writers, open daily approximately 10 AM to 7 PM.

shops.name: Ghirardelli Square
shops.description: The historic 1893 chocolate factory complex at Fisherman's Wharf has been transformed into a shopping and dining destination anchored by the world-famous Ghirardelli Chocolate Company flagship store and ice cream shop.

shops.name: The Cannery at Del Monte Square
shops.description: A historic 1909 Del Monte peach cannery converted into an open-air shopping and dining complex near Fisherman's Wharf, featuring boutiques, galleries, and restaurants.

shops.name: Pier 39 Shops
shops.description: A two-level waterfront marketplace at Fisherman's Wharf offering dozens of specialty shops, San Francisco souvenirs, and bay views, home to the famous sea lion colony on the west docks.
shops.address: Pier 39, Beach Street & Embarcadero, Fisherman's Wharf

shops.name: Only in San Francisco (PIER 39)
shops.type: San Francisco souvenir and gift shop
shops.description: A PIER 39 retailer specializing in San Francisco-themed gifts and souvenirs, which reported July 4th sales up 20% over the prior year during the 2026 Independence Day holiday.

shops.name: Levi's Plaza Shops & Offices
shops.description: The headquarters complex of Levi Strauss & Co. at the northern Embarcadero features a landscaped public plaza and retail amenities along Battery and Sansome streets.

shops.name: Book Passage — Ferry Building
shops.description: The Ferry Building outpost of the Bay Area's beloved independent bookstore, hosting regular author readings and events in the landmark Ferry Building Marketplace.

shops.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
shops.type: Artisan food hall and farmers' market
shops.description: The restored 1898 Ferry Building on the Embarcadero houses dozens of local food purveyors, restaurants, and artisan producers, with a Saturday farmers' market drawing crowds from across the Bay Area.

shops.name: Coppola's Winery Retail — Cafe Zoetrope
shops.description: Attached to Cafe Zoetrope in the landmark Columbus Tower, this retail counter offers bottles and tastings from Francis Ford Coppola's Napa and Sonoma wine estates.

artEntertainment.name: Club Fugazi
artEntertainment.description: The historic 1913 North Beach theater — legendary former home of Beach Blanket Babylon — now hosts "Dear San Francisco," an acclaimed cirque show by The 7 Fingers, with performances through October 2026.

artEntertainment.name: Coit Tower
artEntertainment.type: Historic landmark with WPA murals and observation deck
artEntertainment.description: The 210-foot Art Deco tower atop Telegraph Hill, built in 1933, features New Deal WPA murals depicting California life and an observation deck with 360-degree Bay Area views; open daily 10 AM to 5 PM, elevator tickets $10 adults.

artEntertainment.name: Exploratorium
artEntertainment.description: Housed at Pier 15 on the Embarcadero, the world-renowned Exploratorium offers hundreds of hands-on exhibits spanning science, art, and human perception, with adult-only After Dark Thursdays and regular family programming.

artEntertainment.name: The Beat Museum
artEntertainment.description: Celebrating 20 years in the heart of North Beach, the Beat Museum houses a large collection of Beat Generation memorabilia, personal effects, and manuscripts from Kerouac, Ginsberg, Bukowski, and others.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park
artEntertainment.type: National park maritime museum and historic ships
artEntertainment.description: Located at Hyde Street Pier, this national park includes the world's largest collection of historic ships, the Maritime Museum building, and Aquatic Park, offering free beach access and ticketed ship boarding.

artEntertainment.name: USS Pampanito (SS-383)
artEntertainment.description: A restored World War II fleet submarine moored at Pier 45, open for self-guided tours daily; the Pampanito completed six wartime patrols in the Pacific and is a National Historic Landmark.

artEntertainment.name: Musée Mécanique
artEntertainment.type: Antique arcade and mechanical musical instruments museum
artEntertainment.description: A beloved free-admission Fisherman's Wharf institution housing one of the world's largest privately owned collections of antique coin-operated amusements and mechanical musical instruments.

artEntertainment.name: Aquarium of the Bay
artEntertainment.description: Located at PIER 39, the Aquarium of the Bay features walk-through glass tunnels surrounded by sharks, rays, and thousands of Bay-native marine animals, with a focus on San Francisco Bay ecosystems.

artEntertainment.name: Cobb's Comedy Club
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's premier stand-up comedy venue, hosting nationally touring comedians and local talent in an intimate 400-seat club on Columbus Avenue in North Beach.

artEntertainment.name: City Lights Bookstore — Events & Readings
artEntertainment.description: Beyond its bookstore and publishing house mission, City Lights hosts a crowded calendar of author readings, poetry events, and literary discussions at its historic 261 Columbus Ave location.

gymsRecreation.name: Glow Pilates Yoga Spa
gymsRecreation.type: Pilates, yoga, and wellness spa studio
gymsRecreation.description: A North Beach holistic fitness studio offering Pilates, yoga, and spa services including Red Light Therapy, with a warm community atmosphere welcoming members of all ages.
gymsRecreation.address: North Beach (exact address on website glowyogasf.com)

gymsRecreation.name: Orangetheory Fitness North Beach
gymsRecreation.description: The North Beach location of the national Orangetheory franchise, offering high-intensity interval training classes combining treadmill, rowing, and weight-floor work at 1255 Columbus Ave.

gymsRecreation.name: Fitness SF Embarcadero
gymsRecreation.description: A well-equipped Embarcadero-area gym with a full range of cardio and strength equipment, group fitness classes, and pool access, serving the Financial District and northern waterfront neighborhoods.

gymsRecreation.name: Washington Square Park
gymsRecreation.description: The heart of North Beach, this 2.8-acre park established in 1847 offers open green lawns for picnics, tai chi, and informal recreation, flanked by Saints Peter & Paul Church and surrounded by neighborhood cafés.

gymsRecreation.name: Aquatic Park & Beach
gymsRecreation.type: Public saltwater swimming cove and beach
gymsRecreation.description: A protected saltwater cove within the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park, popular for open-water swimming and sunbathing year-round, home to the Dolphin Club and South End Rowing Club.
gymsRecreation.address: Beach Street at Polk Street, Fisherman's Wharf

gymsRecreation.name: Dolphin Club
gymsRecreation.description: A storied San Francisco institution founded in 1877, the Dolphin Club offers year-round open-water swimming in Aquatic Park Cove, rowing, and sauna access to members.

gymsRecreation.name: South End Rowing Club
gymsRecreation.description: Founded in 1873, the South End Rowing Club is one of San Francisco's oldest athletic clubs, offering open-water rowing, swimming, and handball at Aquatic Park Cove.

gymsRecreation.name: Pioneer Park (Coit Tower Summit)
gymsRecreation.description: The small public park at the apex of Telegraph Hill surrounding Coit Tower, offering some of the most sweeping 360-degree views in San Francisco, accessible via the famous Filbert and Greenwich Steps.

gymsRecreation.name: Filbert Steps & Greenwich Steps
gymsRecreation.description: Two iconic Telegraph Hill stairway trails winding through lush private gardens to the summit, inhabited by San Francisco's famous flock of wild Cherry-headed Conures (parrots).
gymsRecreation.address: Filbert Street at Sansome Street, Telegraph Hill

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Club Gateway
gymsRecreation.description: A premium athletic club near the Embarcadero with a full suite of amenities including pools, tennis, squash courts, group fitness classes, and personal training.
